columns.name: is_fee_revenue_provisional
columns.description: True while this day's fee and revenue columns can still change, which is until they have been read 3 nights after the day ended: the newest two days of a nightly build. revenue.near.org and DefiLlama publish a day before its data has fully arrived, then rewrite it. The page read $9,319 for 2026-11-03 and $164,920 a night later, and DefiLlama follows a night after the page. Leave these days out of trends and totals. Volume columns are not affected. The number comes from few reads (2026-10-28 to 2026-11-05), and a data test fails if a figure moves in the day's first week after the flag clears. False does not mean final for good: a later rewrite of history would show in dq_revisions.

See dq_revisions.

columns.name: is_fee_revenue_provisional
columns.description: True while this day's fees_usd and revenue_usd can still change, by the rule on fct_intents_daily: until they have been read 3 nights after the day ended, so the newest two days of a nightly build. NEAR's fees are mostly Intents fees and settle with them: they read $33,285 for 2026-10-31 and $146,822 two nights later. Every chain gets the same rule, so filtering on this column cuts them all at the same day. The other chains' first reads also run low, by up to about 6% for fees on Ethereum, Solana and Sui, but they have no fixed settling time, so False does not mean settled for them. A data test holds the number for NEAR only.

description: The Bitwise NEAR ETF (NRR) per trading day. Flow is the change in shares times that day's NAV, the same maths as the flows SoSoValue reports. flow_basis says how each row's change was reached. A creation does not prove NEAR was bought on the market that day, because shares can be created for cash or for NEAR. Bitwise's terms limit copying its figures: see registry/sources.csv.
sources: Bitwise's page, SoSoValue through news reports, archival RPC

columns.name: date_day
columns.description: US trading day. The first row, 2026-09-28, is the seed capital, the day before trading began.

columns.name: nav_usd
columns.description: Net asset value per share, from the chart on Bitwise's page. On a day the chart has not reached, net assets divided by shares.

columns.name: market_price_usd
columns.description: Closing market price per share, from the same chart.

columns.name: premium_discount_pct
columns.description: Market price above NAV, or below it if negative.

columns.name: volume_shares
columns.description: Shares traded that day. Starts with the first saved snapshot, because the page shows only the latest day.

columns.name: shares_outstanding
columns.description: Shares at the close. Built from flow_shares through the history file, then taken from Bitwise's page. Empty on a day no snapshot saw.

columns.name: fund_page_shares
columns.description: The share count on Bitwise's page for that day, where a snapshot saw it. A data test holds shares_outstanding to it.

columns.name: net_assets_usd
columns.description: Net assets from Bitwise's page where a snapshot saw that day, otherwise shares_outstanding times nav_usd.

columns.name: near_in_trust
columns.description: NEAR the fund holds. Known where a snapshot saw that day, plus two dates in the history file; on 2026-09-28 it is the seed deposit seen on chain.

columns.name: near_per_share
columns.description: near_in_trust divided by shares_outstanding, carried forward from the last day it was known.

columns.name: flow_shares
columns.description: Shares created, or redeemed if negative, that day. If a night was missed, the next reading's change covers the days between.

columns.name: flow_baskets
columns.description: flow_shares in baskets of 10,000 shares, the size set in the prospectus.

columns.name: flow_usd
columns.description: flow_shares times nav_usd. Empty for the seed capital, because the reported cumulative figures fit only without it.

columns.name: flow_near
columns.description: flow_shares times near_per_share: the NEAR those shares stand for.

columns.name: flow_basis
columns.description: How flow_shares was reached. fund_page: the change in Bitwise's share count. reported: a flow reported by SoSoValue, divided by NAV. cumulative_difference: the gap between two reported cumulative figures. chain_settlement: whole baskets settled on chain the next trading day, an estimate. seed_capital: the prospectus's seed baskets.

columns.name: trading_days_covered
columns.description: Trading days this row's change spans. Above 1 means a night without a snapshot came before it.

columns.name: reported_flow_usd
columns.description: Daily net flow reported by SoSoValue, read from a news report. A cross-check, except where flow_basis is reported.

columns.name: reported_cumulative_usd
columns.description: Cumulative net inflow reported by SoSoValue, read from a news report.

columns.name: reported_net_assets_usd
columns.description: Net assets reported by SoSoValue, read from a news report. A data test holds them to shares_outstanding times nav_usd.

columns.name: staked_share
columns.description: Share of the fund's NEAR that is staked, from Bitwise's page.

columns.name: net_staking_rate
columns.description: Staking reward rate after the fund's staking expenses, from Bitwise's page.

columns.name: source_url
columns.description: The report or filing behind this row in the history file.

columns.name: note
columns.description: How this row in the history file was reached.

description: The Bitwise NEAR ETF's (NRR) NEAR as seen on chain, per UTC day: the wallets Bitwise lists, read inside the fund's staking pool at the first block of the next day. NEAR that moves is rounded to baskets of 10,000 shares. The chain settles about one trading day after the trade and nets orders against each other, so use fct_etf_nrr_daily for what traded on a day. NEAR outside the pool is not counted.
sources: archival RPC, with the wallet list from Bitwise's page

columns.name: date_day
columns.description: UTC calendar day the balances close.

columns.name: block_height
columns.description: The block read: the first of the next UTC day.

columns.name: wallets_in_pool
columns.description: Listed wallets holding at least 1 NEAR in the pool.

columns.name: near_in_wallets
columns.description: NEAR staked or unstaking in the pool across the listed wallets.

columns.name: near_unstaking
columns.description: The part of near_in_wallets that has been unstaked and not yet withdrawn.

columns.name: rewards_near
columns.description: Growth in wallets that changed by under 0.1% that day, which is staking rewards.

columns.name: moved_near
columns.description: All other change in those balances: NEAR deposited, or withdrawn if negative.

columns.name: settled_shares
columns.description: moved_near as whole baskets of 10,000 shares. Redemptions are negative.

columns.name: left_over_near
columns.description: The part of moved_near that does not make a whole basket, such as a small rebalance.

columns.name: running_settled_shares
columns.description: settled_shares added up since launch, to compare with the fund's share count.

columns.name: moved_value_usd
columns.description: moved_near at that day's NEAR price from fct_market_daily. Empty until the price is in.

columns.name: pool_near
columns.description: All NEAR delegated to the pool, including other delegators.

columns.name: share_of_circulating_supply
columns.description: near_in_wallets divided by circulating supply from fct_market_daily.

columns.name: snapshot_date
columns.description: Snapshot the day was read in. Past blocks do not change, so a later read gives the same balances.

description: Commits and active authors per tracked repository per week. A fixed repository list, not a whole-ecosystem count; GitHub's author list covers each repository's top 100. Both measures are empty for a repository whose year of readings is all zero although GitHub says it was pushed to in that year, because GitHub's statistics endpoints serve zeros for some very large repositories (anza-xyz/agave on 2026-11-01).

columns.name: commits
columns.description: Commits that week. Empty where GitHub served a year of zeros for a repository it reports as pushed to; see the table description.

columns.name: active_authors
columns.description: Authors with at least one commit that week, among GitHub's top 100 for the repository.

description: Stars, forks and last push per tracked repository, per read.
NEAR Catalog entries per read, for counting projects by tag over time.
Engagement on the tracked governance threads, per read. Governance outcomes belong in dim_event.

House of Stake proposals read directly from vote.dao, as of the newest snapshot. A status of Voting means the numbers are still moving. Test and spam proposals are kept; filter them on status or title.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Contract status, such as Created, Rejected, Voting, Succeeded or Defeated.

columns.name: link
columns.description: Discussion link given in the proposal.

columns.name: voting_start_date
columns.description: Date voting opened. Empty if it never opened.

columns.name: for_venear
columns.description: veNEAR voting for: the first option in the contract's vote list.

columns.name: against_venear
columns.description: veNEAR voting against: the second option.

columns.name: eligible_venear
columns.description: Total veNEAR in the proposal's snapshot.

columns.name: quorum_threshold
columns.description: Share of eligible veNEAR required for quorum.

columns.name: approval_threshold
columns.description: Share of votes required to pass.

description: House of Stake participation per snapshot, read directly from venear.dao.
Every place two sources should agree, side by side. A gap beyond tolerance must have a written explanation, or make verify fails.

columns.name: subject
columns.description: What the check is about, when it runs per account.

columns.name: diff_pct
columns.description: Absolute gap as a percentage of the larger value.

columns.name: independence
columns.description: independent, or same_upstream when both sources read the same data, so agreement proves little.

columns.name: explanation
columns.description: Why the gap exists, from registry/reconciliation_notes.csv.

description: How current each daily dataset is, relative to the newest snapshot the build can see.

Values a source changed after first publishing them, comparing the oldest and newest snapshot of the same key. This shows that a value moved, not when or how often; to date a change, compare consecutive snapshots in silver.

columns.name: change_pct
columns.description: Change from first to last, as a percentage.

description: How each dataset fared on each run date: ok, partial, skipped or failed, and why.

columns.name: detail
columns.description: Why, when it was not ok.

description: Where the data came from, per dataset and snapshot. Cite this next to a chart so a reader can find the exact responses behind it.

columns.name: declared_rows
columns.description: Rows, where the fetcher recorded them.

columns.name: example_url
columns.description: One URL read for this dataset.

columns.name: first_fetched_at
columns.description: When the first file was fetched.

columns.name: last_fetched_at
columns.description: When the last file was fetched.

columns.name: note
columns.description: Any change made before saving, such as trimming.
